AgriFresh Foods - Q3 FY2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AgriFresh Foods Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you're using a landline or the button provided if on webcast. To withdraw your question, press star then two. We ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss AgriFresh Foods' Q3 FY2024 results. Joining me on the call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Growth Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 FY2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on four key areas: overall company performance highlights, organic revenue growth overall and by region, organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and full year, and capital expenditure plans and priorities.

First, regarding overall company performance highlights: We posted net revenues of $3.25 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with 9% organic growth from 4% volume and 5% net pricing, plus a boost from acquisitions like BioVita. Adjusted gross margins expanded 150 basis points sequentially to 34.8%, operating income rose 18% to $485 million, and adjusted EPS hit $0.92, up 28%. Our beverages and snacks segments led the way, with regional strength across North America, EMEA, and emerging markets.

Second, concerning organic revenue growth overall and by region: We achieved 6.8% overall organic growth, accelerating from last year, driven by 3.2 points from pricing and 3.6 from volume/mix. North America grew 8.4%, EMEA 4.2%, Asia-Pacific 7.1%, and Latin America 5.9%, fueled by innovation in functional beverages and snacks, plus e-commerce gains.

Third, in terms of organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter/year: For Q4, we expect 3% to 4% organic growth, with pricing at 2 to 2.5 points and volume/mix 1 to 1.5 points from new launches and distribution. For full-year FY2025, we're raising to 4% to 5%, supported by pricing discipline, innovation pipeline, and regional momentum.

Finally, looking at capital expenditure plans and priorities: We're guiding FY2024 capex to $525 million, up 12%, focused on capacity expansion, automation, sustainability, and supply chain resilience to drive long-term ROIC above 10%.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Lisa Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 FY2024. Net sales were $3.25 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 34.8%, impacted positively by hedging and procurement savings despite input cost inflation. Operating income was $485 million, and earnings per share were $0.92 adjusted diluted. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.2 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases—we repurchased 2.1 million shares for $120 million this quarter under our $1 billion program.

Let me expand on the highlights Mike touched on, starting with our overall company performance. This quarter marks our ninth straight quarter of double-digit revenue growth, blending top-line momentum, margin expansion, and disciplined execution across beverages, snacks, and plant-based convenience foods. Our brands like AquaPure hydration and NutriCrunch snacks showed resilience amid input cost inflation, health trends, and elevated freight. Adjusted EBITDA reached $580 million, or 17.8% of sales, with A&P efficient at 11.2% of revenue thanks to digital campaigns boosting e-commerce to 18%. Free cash flow was $320 million, or 110% of adjusted net income, funding $200 million in dividends and deleveraging to 2.3x net debt-to-EBITDA. 

In segments, beverages grew 15% to $1.3 billion on 7% volume in functional hydration and RTD coffee, capturing 2.2 share points. Snacks & convenience rose 10% to $1.14 billion, leading in better-for-you with #1 velocity. North America delivered 14% growth via club channels, EMEA 11% organically on plant-based yogurts gaining 1.5 share points against Danone's Alpro, and APAC/LatAm 8% despite China softness, offset by Indonesia tea JV. Our HealthForward 2025 initiative launched 12 plant-based SKUs, AI forecasting cut inventory 18%, and ESG progress includes 22% emissions drop, earning Dow Jones Sustainability Index recognition. Challenges like 5-6% labor inflation and 40% cocoa spikes are managed via hedging. We reaffirm FY2024 guidance: 8-10% organic growth, 18%+ EBITDA margins, $3.45-$3.55 EPS.

Turning deeper into organic revenue growth for the quarter, we delivered overall organic revenue growth of 6.8%, our eighth consecutive positive quarter, accelerating 110 basis points from 5.7% in Q3 FY2023. This excludes our low-margin European canned goods divestiture and forex tailwinds, spotlighting core snacks, beverages, and prepared foods health. Pricing added 3.2 points amid 12-15% rises in cocoa, sugar, and dairy, with 85% hedging keeping gross margins at 42.1%, ahead of Mondelez and Hershey. Volume/mix contributed 3.6 points, with 1.2 U.S. snack share gains per NielsenIQ on CoreCrunch baked snacks at 14% penetration via Walmart/Kroger. Innovation drove $45 million from VitaBoost RTD functionals, up 28% sequentially in the 11% growing category per IRI, plus 22% e-commerce now 18% of revenues via Amazon AI personalization.

Regionally, North America, 52% of revenue, grew 8.4% organically, accelerating from 6.9%, led by 5.1 volume/mix points on ZestBites nuts gaining 220 bps ACV, 3.3 pricing, Costco GreenSip alt-dairy share from Chobani, and 65% premium growth. EMEA, 28%, hit 4.2% despite sentiment softness, pricing 4.8 points on PureFlow waters at 22% UK share per Kantar, slight volume dip offset by Farm-to-Table snacks boosting loyalty 15% and SpiceRush Gulf flavors adding $18 million. Asia-Pacific, 15%, surged 7.1% from 3.8%, volume/mix 4.9 points on QuickMunch noodles at 25% distribution in India/Indonesia via Reliance, 2.2 pricing amid rice/palm volatility, TropiChill juices up 32% in China. Latin America, 5%, 5.9% resilient amid Argentina 140% inflation/Brazil FX, 4.2 volume/mix on FrescaFizz EDLP gaining 1.5 share, 1.7 pricing, Mexico micro-hub drone delivery at 92% availability for 18% growth. FY2024 organic outlook 6-6.5%, Q4 holiday ramps, SKU rationalization for 50+ FY2025 innovations in protein snacks/zero-sugar RTDs, Global Harvest Network 70% renewables for 100-150 bps margin gains.

Before Q&A, let's discuss organic sales growth guidance, a cornerstone of our strategy. Q3 delivered 4.2% organic growth, ahead of guide, with 2.8 pricing points offsetting cocoa/dairy/edible oils inflation like Nestlé/Hershey, flat to +0.5% volumes on HealthWise bars/plant-based up 12%, lapping post-pandemic comps. For Q4, expect 3.0-4.0% organic net revenue growth—reported excluding M&A/FX—pricing 2.0-2.5 points, especially 3-4% salty snacks hikes for palm oil, volume/mix 1.0-1.5 points from ZestQuench zero-sugar electrolytes vs. Prime/Gatorade tracking $150 million on 15% R&D hike, 2,500 NA club points at Costco/Sam's, e-commerce 18% vs. 12% last year per Nielsen. North America 65% sales: 3.5-4.5%, EmberChip +1.2 share vs. Utz/Lay's; EMEA 20%: 2.0-3.0%, UK softness offset by 8% German/French plant dairy; APAC/LatAm 15%: 4.0-5.0%, Indonesia/Brazil hydration packs/local packs.

For FY2025, raising to 4.0-5.0% from 3.5-4.5%, conviction in Health Forward, Value Smart with 150bps share gains per IRI/Circana. Pricing 2.5-3.0 points vs. 4-6% COGS inflation—down from 8% FY24—via negotiations/70% cocoa hedge like Mondelez 300bps recovery. Volume/mix 1.5-2.0 from $500 million pipeline, 25% SKUs lower sugar/Na like FruitBurst vs. EU labels, recyclable packs +20% Gen Z repeats. Productivity $120 million Supply Chain 2.0 AI yields, NielsenIQ digital +10% velocity. Beverages 40% portfolio +6% vs. snacks 3%, kombucha/functional water 15% US conv share, +50bps margins. NA 4.5-5.5% premium nuts +18% gifting; EMEA 3.5-4.5% clean yogurt Danone-style; APAC/LatAm 5.5-6.5% Brazil ceviche chips +7%. Risks: US unemployment >4.2% -1pt volumes, avian flu, FX; mitigated by $300 million WC efficiency, 2.1x leverage. Underpins FY25 adj EPS $3.45-$3.55, 8-10% growth, organic/share gains/capital discipline.

On capital expenditures, FY2024 $525 million, +12% from $468 million FY2023, targeting 10-12% ROIC, 3.5-year paybacks for 6-8% volumes in beverages 52%/snacks 38% amid easing but elevated commodities. Pillars align with functional bev 25% CAGR, EU PPWR recyclability.

Manufacturing 40% ~$210 million: $120 million Ho Chi Minh greenfield 250k sq ft NutriGlow RTD +20% capacity Vietnam $2.5B 12% sports market like Pepsi APAC; $50 million Fresno oat lattes +15% 18% category Nielsen; $40 million São Paulo guava energy vs. Monster +2.5 share. Addresses 92% utilization FMI.

Automation/digital 25% ~$131 million: $75 million RPA/AI FANUC robots ProteinBar pouches 25% labor lift/30% downtime Siemens IoT; $56 million SAP S/4HANA AI demand sensing +15% accuracy vs. bullwhip, GDPR low-sugar Europe 35% labor COGS.

Sustainability/ESG 20% ~$105 million: $60 million solar/heat pumps 25% renewables FY25 Unilever-like; $25 million water closed-loop -20% AWS California; $20 million rPET mono AquaVita -40% virgin Coke World Without Waste, $15 million savings/10% premium GenZ Deloitte 65% priority.

Supply chain 15% ~$79 million: $40 million micro-fulfillment US Midwest/Mumbai Shopify D2C; $20 million reefer electric/IBM blockchain 99.9% perishables yogurt; JIT vendor portals 15% WC. NA 55% automation 4% volumes; EMEA 25% sustain PPWR; APAC/LATAM 20% capacity 10%+.

FY2025 capex $550-575 million, 5% M&A nutrition tuck-ins, 9-11% EBITDA, 12-15% EPS CAGR to 2027—growth/cost/future-proof.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for 8-10% organic revenue growth, adjusted EBITDA margins of 18%+, and adjusted EPS of $3.45-$3.55.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Good morning, John. Inflation remains a key focus, but our hedging covers 85% of key inputs like cocoa, sugar, dairy, and palm oil, capping COGS at 2.5% rise versus industry 7-9%. We've executed disciplined pricing—4-5% across portfolio—recovering margins while volumes hold via mix to health premiums. Procurement savings added $45 million sequentially through supplier networks, similar to peers. We're navigating cocoa's 40% spike and labor 5-6% via productivity, positioning for FY25 4-6% COGS inflation with 70% hedges locked favorably.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Emily Rodriguez (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for new product launches and what is the expected impact?

Raj Patel (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. Our $500 million innovation pipeline is firing on all cylinders, with Q4 launches like ZestQuench zero-sugar electrolytes targeting $150 million incremental, directly challenging Prime and Gatorade in functionals growing 11% IRI. VitaBoost nootropics added $45 million this quarter, up 28%, and PlantPower oat variants/EmberChip snacks drive 12% category growth. FY25 brings 20+ SKUs—protein bars, low-sugar gummies, guava energy—reformulated 25% lower Na/sugar for EU regs, plus sustainability packs boosting Gen Z 20% repeats. Expect 1.5-2.0 points volume/mix uplift, 50bps margin expansion, 150bps share gains per IRI/Circana in $100B alt-protein wave.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

David Lee (Morgan Stanley):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Elena Vargas (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, David. Our Supply Chain 2.0 program delivered $120 million productivity via AI yield optimization at three plants, digital shelf NielsenIQ +10% velocity. Capex $79 million fortifies: micro-fulfillment US/Mumbai for Red Sea 30% freight spikes, IBM blockchain/reefer electric for 99.9% perishables, vendor JIT 15% WC efficiency. Regional hubs like Mexico drones 92% availability, Vietnam greenfield +20% RTD, Fresno retrofits. Global Harvest 70% renewables, Palantir AI forecasting -18% inventory to 45 days. Mitigates avian flu/FX/geopolitics, utilization 92% FMI, on track net-zero 2040.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Laura Kim with Barclays. Please proceed.

Laura Kim (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Lisa Chen (CFO):
Thanks, Laura. Q4 organic 3-4%, accelerating FY24 to 6-6.5% overall, holiday merchandising/new ramps. FY25 raised 4-5%, 2.5-3 pricing/1.5-2 volume-mix, NA 4.5-5.5%, EMEA 3.5-4.5%, APAC/LatAm 5.5-6.5%. EPS $3.45-3.55, 8-10% growth. Capex supports ROIC 10-12%, deleveraging 2.1x, dividends/repurchases. Risks modeled—unemployment, flu, FX—but $300 million WC buffers, innovation/distribution fuel outperformance in consolidating F&B.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in AgriFresh Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
